paragraphs: Friend, this chapter is a lot of kings. Three months, eleven years, three months, eleven years, and a crown that keeps changing heads. But look at what the LORD did the whole time. "Again and again the LORD, the God of their fathers, sent word to His people through His messengers because He had compassion on them" (2 Chronicles 36:15).

Here's the lesson, and it's a heavy one. They "mocked the messengers of God, despising His words and scoffing at His prophets, until the wrath of the LORD against His people was stirred up beyond remedy" (2 Chronicles 36:16). I think that's one of the saddest lines in the whole chapter. God's warnings were never the problem. They were a gift from a God who had compassion, and the people kept treating them like junk mail.

But the chapter doesn't end in the ashes, and THAT is the good news. Seventy years later, the word of the LORD through Jeremiah comes true right on time, and the LORD stirs the spirit of Cyrus, king of Persia, to say His people "may go up" (2 Chronicles 36:22-23). I know a little about being shoved in the dark and thinking it's over, and let me tell you, the One who keeps His word is the One who comes and gets you. So listen when He speaks, baker, because He always keeps His word, and His word is where the way home begins.
